text: The stakeholder's ask was before the eight AM leadership meeting, not at eight AM sharp. A Schedule trigger set for five AM gives the whole pipeline three real hours of margin — covering the source query, the data flow's Spark cluster startup, and the retry policy from Lesson 55 actually needing to use its retries on a genuinely bad night.
Building in margin here is a deliberate design choice, not laziness — a pipeline that only just barely makes an eight AM deadline on a good night has no room left for a bad one.

Lesson 54 already put the SQL connection string behind Key Vault. Two more real gaps close out the security requirement: the sink's credentials get the exact same Key Vault treatment as the source, and RBAC on the resource group gives Data Factory Contributor only to the on-call team, with Reader for everyone else who needs visibility but shouldn't be able to accidentally edit a production pipeline.

The Monitor hub answers did last night's run succeed. For the kind of long-term visibility a real production pipeline actually needs, Chapter 8's Log Analytics routing applies directly. This single query turns seems to be working fine into an actual, verifiable thirty-day reliability trend — something Northwind's team can check without relying on memory or anecdote.

Before walking through the finished pipeline in the next lesson, every item on this checklist should genuinely be true: scheduled with real margin, every credential behind Key Vault, RBAC properly scoped, diagnostics flowing to Log Analytics, and a scoped alert watching for real failures.

Scheduled with real margin, secured end to end, and genuinely observable over time — not just working today. Next: Present the Finished Pipeline — explaining exactly what you built, clearly, to someone who's never seen a single piece of it.
